candidate_matrix.reason: Raw evidence cleanup can break auditability and requires explicit preservation proof plus Norven approval before any cleanup apply.

candidate_matrix.reason: Layer A inclusion/exclusion is a Norven-reserved product decision and cannot be delegated to Cap or Prism.

candidate_matrix.title: Formal release readiness convergence assessment
candidate_matrix.reason: Claude Code selected this as the safest zero-destruction path. Cap adjudicates this as P4-18 because it consolidates all remaining blocker gaps before choosing any delete-last, raw evidence cleanup or human product decision path.

selected_next_slice.title: R1 formal release readiness convergence assessment after Prism report archive apply
scope: Synthesize internal-control-plane, prism-layer-and-evidence, Layer A product boundary and package surface status into one release-readiness gap map.
Rank the remaining safe implementation slices after P4-16.
Identify which remaining actions require Norven/manual approval before execution.
Do not delete or retire old prism/reports anchors.
Do not clean or prune prism/runs raw evidence.
Do not decide Layer A product scope.
Do not change release switches, package privacy, registry or license.
minimum_acceptance: human-readable report with current release blockers and safe next slices
Prism review by Claude Code and Kimi when available
P4-15 guard and P4-16 apply checker still pass after P4-17 report addition

adjudication.reason: Claude Code recommended release readiness convergence; Kimi recommended old-anchor delete-last preflight. Cap selected convergence first because P4-17 follows a long localized Prism-report archive sequence, and a non-destructive global gap map is safer before any old-anchor retirement, raw evidence cleanup or human product decision path.
adjudication.tie_breaker: When one option continues a local implementation chain and another option creates a non-destructive whole-release gap map after many local slices, choose the global gap map unless a blocker requires immediate local execution.
